title: Problem while using jackson @JsonNaming in AWS Lambda
body:
I am trying to implement a @JsonNaming for a class which serializes a json property `blog_title` by a field named `blogTitle`. This is the sample [URL](https://run.mocky.io/v3/f55b5437-2360-4ccd-aee3-e6655dec87ce) that I am trying to parse the JSON  to an object. 

```java
@JsonNaming(PropertyNamingStrategy.SnakeCaseStrategy.class)
@JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown = true)
@RegisterForReflection
public class SampleResponse {
    private String blogTitle;

    public SampleResponse() {
    }

    public String getBlogTitle() {
        return blogTitle;
    }

    public void setBlogTitle(String blogTitle) {
        this.blogTitle = blogTitle;
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return "SampleResponse{" +
            "blogTitle='" + blogTitle + '\'' +
            '}';
    }
}
```



**Expected behavior**
Normally it works correctly in quarkus:dev mode without any issue but when I deploy it in AWS Lambda (serverless) it throws an error of no default constructor.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a simple class which contains `@JsonNaming(PropertyNamingStrategy.SnakeCaseStrategy.class)`
2. Put a dependency for Jackson 
```xml
<dependency>
      <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
      <artifactId>quarkus-resteasy-jackson</artifactId>
</dependency>
```
3. Implement a simple json parsing using jackson which has a json property in snake style format i.e "blog_title" 
4. Build it for native and aws lambda support
5. Execute the lambda function and it throws an error.

**Configuration**
```properties
# Add your application.properties here, if applicable.
sample/mp-rest/url=https://run.mocky.io/v3
```
